task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from player talent and possession counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and possession counts?
Does talent control behave adequately when role coverage is measured per lineup?
What risks arise from deriving role labels from play-type possession records?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned no records, so no earlier study by this project on lineup role coverage, role-label validity, or talent control is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage of organizer, shaper, or terminal roles varies within team in these data.
Whether the role constructs are reliable or valid as measured.
Whether talent control adequately separates role coverage from talent in lineup-level data.
Whether any earlier approach to this question succeeded or failed.
own_inferences: The data description lists play-type possession records with initiator, play type, and points, so role labels would likely be built from play-type and scoring information. If points enter the label definition, coverage will partly encode outcome, which is a leakage and circularity risk.
Within-team variation is testable with team-season fixed effects over 90 team-seasons, but lineup exposure is uneven, so many lineups may have too few possessions for stable coverage estimates.
Coverage and talent are likely correlated because starters and high-usage players tend to fill the same roles, so separability depends on the variance left in coverage after talent is partialled out.
The 2025-26 season and playoffs are partial before 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so including them without a cutoff would mix complete and incomplete data.
uncertainties: The operational definitions of organizer, shaper, and terminal are not given in the task statement; the glossary was not consulted.
The talent proxy is not specified; its reliability and whether it is measured out of sample are unknown.
Achievable power depends on the number of lineup-stints with adequate possession counts, which was not reported.
No historical records exist, so there is no evidence on whether the constructs replicate.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieval returned no records, so it neither supported nor blocked the decision. The decision rests on the task description and the listed data. The main reason to proceed with changes is that the within-team, team-season design can be run on the listed data, but only after the role definitions and talent proxy are fixed in advance.

blocking_constraints.text: If role labels use points or shot results, coverage is partly defined by the outcome it is meant to predict, so any association is partly circular.
Many lineups have few possessions, so coverage and outcome estimates may be too noisy at the lineup level unless stints are pooled.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. This is not evidence that it has not been answered.

risks.text: Role labels built from play type, initiator, or points can encode the outcome, so coverage may predict points by construction.
Coverage correlates with talent, usage, and roster position, so talent control may not fully separate them.
Role coverage and the talent proxy may have low reliability across seasons, which attenuates estimates and weakens separability tests.
With 90 team-seasons, within-team contrasts in coverage may be too few to detect modest effects after multiple lineup and role terms are included.
Low-minute lineups produce unstable coverage and outcome estimates.
Using full-season or playoff data to define labels or talent for games already played would leak future information.
Testing three roles, several coverage definitions, and several talent proxies creates many comparisons.
Rule and play-style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may change role definitions and base rates over time.
Coverage levels and outcome rates may differ strongly across teams and seasons, affecting interpretation.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup-stint coverage of at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal role and possession-level points per possession, conditional on a pre-specified out-of-sample talent proxy, with the separability of coverage from talent and counts reported as a separate quantity.
design.unit: Lineup stint (five-player unit within a team-game, aggregated to lineup-team-season) with possession-level outcomes nested inside.
design.sample: Complete regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25, with playoffs analyzed separately. Include 2025-26 regular season only if the run is on or after 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs only if on or after 2026-06-21. Exclude partial data. Keep lineups above a minimum possession threshold fixed before analysis.
design.power: Not yet computed. Before locking, run a simulation on the observed lineup-possession distribution to find the detectable effect size at the chosen threshold, with the 90 team-seasons as the clustering unit.
design.controls: Team-season fixed effects for within-team contrasts. Talent proxy computed from prior-season or out-of-sample data, not the same games. Possession counts and minutes as covariates. Lineup random effects. Role definitions fixed in advance and independent of points, with scoring excluded from label construction, or with a sensitivity analysis that excludes scoring-based labels.
design.falsification: Specify in advance that the coverage association should vanish when the outcome is replaced by a non-scoring outcome such as turnover rate, and that a placebo role set with shuffled initiators should show no association. Separability fails if coverage is predicted by talent with R-squared above a pre-set threshold.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary coverage definition and one primary talent proxy. Treat the other role and proxy variants as secondary, with a correction such as Holm across the secondary tests.
design.decision_rule: Report the primary association with a confidence interval and the separability metric. Call the question supported only if the association is positive, the interval excludes zero, the effect survives the falsification checks, and separability is adequate. Call it untestable if the power simulation shows the minimum detectable effect is implausibly large, and rejected if the powered null interval excludes meaningful effects.
design.data_version: Data as of 2026-07-13: complete 2022-23 through 2024-25 seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season only if complete (on or after 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs only if complete (on or after 2026-06-21). Freeze the snapshot and record the version.
